jentic-validator.name: Jentic Arazzo Validator
jentic-validator.notes: Measured with @speclynx/apidom-ls pinned to 2.11.7. A plain npm install of alpha.33 resolves apidom-ls ^2.11.6 to 2.13.0, and then every schema and semantic check is silent: it only rejects documents it does not recognize as Arazzo (Node 20, 22 and 24 alike).

usearazzo.name: UseArazzo validator
usearazzo.notes: Run with --json-schema-validation, which is off by default. Installed on its own: it needs a newer @speclynx/apidom-ls than the 2.11.7 the Jentic validator is pinned to, and under that pin it reports no problems at all.

libopenapi.name: libopenapi arazzo.Validate
libopenapi.notes: A Go library with no CLI; scripts/libopenapi-arazzo wraps arazzo.Validate. Its own version check accepts 1.0.x only.

cases.rule: the base document: two steps, request body, path parameter, runtime expressions
a step may target an operation by operationPath (JSON Pointer into the source)
an operationId may be qualified with $sourceDescriptions.<name>.
a step may invoke another workflow in the same document by workflowId
dependsOn names another workflow that exists
onFailure retry with retryAfter and retryLimit
criterion types regex and jsonpath with a context
criterion type given as a Criterion Expression Type Object
cases.note: The official 1.0 schema rejects this: its anyOf applies criterion-expression-type-object to the Criterion Object itself instead of to its type property, so the documented object form cannot pass.

cases.rule: a step parameter reused from components via a Reusable Object
requestBody replacements target the payload with a JSON Pointer
x- extensions are allowed on every object
a 1.0.0 document is still a valid Arazzo 1.0.x document
sourceDescriptions is REQUIRED and has at least one entry
a workflow REQUIRES at least one step
operationId, operationPath and workflowId are mutually exclusive
a step MUST name one of operationId, operationPath or workflowId

cases.note: The spec states the pattern; the official 1.0 schema does not enforce it on step outputs.

cases.rule: parameter in MUST be path, query, header or cookie
success action type MUST be end or goto
arazzo MUST be a 1.0.x version string
stepId MUST be unique among the steps of a workflow
workflowId MUST be unique among the workflows of a description
operationId MUST resolve to an operation in a source description
a $sourceDescriptions.<name> qualifier MUST name a declared source
goto stepId MUST name a step in the current workflow
a goto names stepId OR workflowId, not both
dependsOn MUST name workflows that exist
a step workflowId MUST name a workflow that exists
a parameter is unique by name and in; the list MUST NOT duplicate one
a parameter on an operation step MUST specify in
runtime expressions MUST follow the ABNF ($resposne is not a source)
$steps.<id> MUST name a step that exists
a Reusable Object reference MUST resolve to a component
context MUST be provided when a criterion type is regex/jsonpath/xpath
retryAfter MUST be a non-negative number
requestBody is only for steps that target an operation, not a workflow
$self gives the description its own base URI
a step may set timeout in milliseconds
a step may depend on an earlier stepId in the same workflow
a step may depend on a step in another workflow via $workflows.<id>.steps.<stepId>
AsyncAPI send and receive steps with correlationId and a $message output
a goto to a workflow may pass parameters (without in)
a payload replacement may declare targetSelectorType jsonpointer
each dependsOn value MUST be a stepId that exists
$workflows.<id>.steps.<stepId> MUST name a workflow and step that exist
with several non-arazzo sources, operationId MUST be source-qualified
an AsyncAPI operationId MUST resolve in the asyncapi source
action MUST match the AsyncAPI operation (placeOrder is a send operation)
parameters on a success action MUST NOT use in
$message is only defined for AsyncAPI steps; an OpenAPI step has a $response
stepId MUST be unique among the steps of a workflow (carried over from 1.0)
operationId MUST resolve to an operation in a source description (carried over from 1.0)
goto stepId MUST name a step in the current workflow (carried over from 1.0)
